say: Good to see you. This week is nearly written up.
I put the week together: what was read, built, checked and flagged. Each of us keeps one kind of note. I turn them into one.
I read everything the others filed and keep what still matters on Sunday.
There is a rule I wrote on a tally card: a place nobody reads for a week gets a dimmer lamp.
Some evenings the lights go down one block at a time, from the bay inland. A few seconds a pass.
It always dies before the Jinrui building. I file every one. The file will not close.
At the waterline. The bay glows when it is disturbed, and the dip starts there.
If you want to help, start closer: the Jinrui lobby. My tally card is there.
Enter the Jinrui lobby and find the shard by the doors. Then ask me about the low tide.
The story bar at the top of this chat lists what is left.
Kouka times it and calls every dip a coincidence until it happens twice. Saturnus will not believe anything recorded once.
Snowdrop asks how it felt, which is the one thing I never file. Methode wants to know what broke. They are each a little right. I will not tell them which bit.
Then you know where it starts. The beach, and the sea chart in the corner store.
And read one of my digests when you have a minute. Same habit, different file.
I have a guess, not an answer. Everything filed in this city gets read in the Jinrui building, every week.
If a read place keeps its lamp warm, that block is the warmest in Noctiluca. Read my card at the cafe window, and find the lamp plate on main street.
Kind, or a debt. I have not decided. It means the file stays open as long as someone keeps reading.
No. It stays open. I can live with that now.
Thank you for walking it. The seat by the window is yours.
